title: Project 3: student record manager

understand.concept: A student record manager stores multiple records, supports adding and listing records, validates fields and may persist records in a file. The project should define limits for names, IDs and record counts.
understand.whyItMatters: This project integrates structures, arrays, functions, input handling and file I/O into a realistic record-oriented program.
understand.analogy: Treat the project or language feature as a set of components with explicit interfaces and responsibilities.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy does not replace C's formal language, library and resource-management rules.

explain.narrative:
A student record manager stores multiple records, supports adding and listing records, validates fields and may persist records in a file. The project should define limits for names, IDs and record counts.

For a complete implementation, define input constraints, ownership, error handling and test cases before coding. Compile with warnings and verify normal, boundary and failure behaviour.

examples.title: Focused C example
examples.explanation: The structure groups an identifier and a fixed-capacity name. The example demonstrates one record; a complete manager needs collection management and input validation.

practise.guidedTask: Identify the capacity limit for the name field.
practise.independentTask: Build add, list, find and save operations. Test duplicate IDs, full storage and invalid names.
hints: Use fgets for bounded line input and define how overlong lines are handled.
Choose whether records live in a fixed array or dynamically allocated collection.
Validate uniqueness and required fields before saving.
